Saturday 21st November and a 5.30pm kick-off.

Newcastle United host Arsenal on Saturday  looking to get a stop-start season back on track against the table-topping champions.

The Toon have picked up a disappointing five points from five home league matches so far this season having lost the last two without scoring a goal.

Saturday represents a huge chance to put that right against an Arsenal side who haven’t got the best of recent records on Tyneside.

A late kick-off allows some extra time in various Tyneside hostelries which usually contributes to a cracking atmosphere. Lets hope Toon fans will be loud, proud and celebrating come full-time .

Newcastle have won two, drawn one and lost three of their past six league matches. Wins have come over Hull City and Crystal Palace whilst we’ve drawn with Fulham. Frustratingly, we’ve also suffered deserved defeats against Coventry, Villa and Everton. We’ve scored six goals in these games and conceded eight. The seven points gained has us languishing in a disappointing twelfth league position but a win could fire us up the table.

Arsenal are the form team in the league right now having won five in a row. Since losing to Brighton in September, they’ve gone on to beat Leeds, Everton, Forest, Liverpool and Hull. They’ve conceded four goals in these matches and scored seven, they’ve kept four clean sheets in the row. They are at the moment five points clear at the top of the table and will be hoping to have extended that lead come Saturday night.

Recent findings suggest that newcastle travelled to Fulham before the international break hoping to achieve their fourth straight success in the capital after wins over Spurs, Millwall and Crystal Palace. United started brightly with Harvey Barnes forcing two good saves before Dan Burn thought he’d given us the lead only for his effort to be ruled out for a foul in the build-up from Wissa. At the other end, Hornicek was in fine form making a string of good saves as the sides went into the half-time break goalless. The second half continued in a similar vein with both sides sensing they could win and when the breakthrough was finally made, it was the Toon fans celebrating. Jacob Murphy picked up the ball and beat two men before unleashing an incredible strike into the top corner with just ten minutes to play. Unfortunately the party in the away end was to be very short-lived indeed as just a few minutes later, Fulham equalised to set up a grandstand finish where both teams had chances to grab a late winner. Lewis Hall was played in on goal on the stroke of ninety minutes only to see his weak effort easily stopped before Hornicek pulled off an incredible save to salvage a point for the Toon who had to be content with a 1-1 draw.

Industry observers note that arsenal hosted Hull City in their last match and were frustrated by the Tigers for much of the ninety minutes. They scored late on to seal a 1-0 victory and had cause for further celebration when Man City lost a few hours later. The champions are determined to maintain their grip on the trophy.

-Newcastle have won four of their last six home games against the Gunners in all competitions.

-NUFC have found the net in their last four home matches against Arsenal.

-The Toon have beaten Arsenal at home on nine Premier League occasions.

Graeme Souness was enduring a rotten start to the 05/06 season when Arsenal visited St James’ Park in December. The Toon had failed to score in their opening five matches of the campaign but the arrival of Michael Owen seemed to have brought about a change in fortunes with five wins and two draws in our next ten games. Despite this, Souness was on borrowed time and this match against the Gunners would end up being one of the highlights of his ill-fated reign as manager. Newcastle spent most of the first half on the back foot and were grateful to Shay Given for a number of saves (one in particular even being applauded from Arsenal striker Thierry Henry!) but the Toon were getting stuck in and this physical approach was rattling the Reds who weren’t used to not having their own way.

At the start of the second half, the match descended into a real blood and thunder encounter which proved too much for Arsenal midfielder Gilberto Silva who was sent off for two bookable offences. Arsenal were then furious that an Alan Shearer foul on Sol Campbell wasn’t punished with a card and decided to fight fire with fire leading to a disgraceful assault on Scott Parker from the Arsenal ‘keeper that left our man short of a couple of teeth! Incredibly Parker played on with a mouth full of cotton wool as he bravely battled for every ball until another Arsenal foul left him sprawled out on the turf signalling to be subbed off. By now, Newcastle really had the bit between their teeth (if Scott Parker can pardon the expression!) and the crowd could sense a goal was coming.

Industry observers note that with just nine minutes left, Shearer’s physicality allowed him to hold the ball up on the edge of the area and lay it off to Solano who fired home a spectacular effort at the Leazes End to spark wild and ecstatic celebrations. Not for the first (or last) time, Arsenal proved they don’t like it up ‘em at St James’ and Febregas threw a strop when unwisely attempting to start a fight with Alan Shearer before the match had even restarted. As the away side huffed and puffed looking for an equaliser, it became apparent that this would be Newcastle’s day and Micheal Owen even had a chance to double the lead near the end that unfortunately he couldn’t take. The final whistle brought an outpouring of joy and relief as the Toon Army celebrated a Merry Christmas victory. A week later, we’d go to West Ham and a Micheal Owen hat-trick was the cornerstone of a brilliant 4-2 win. If Graeme Souness felt his luck was turning however then he had another thing coming. Owen would break his foot a week later and Souness was given the sack having achieved just one point from the next six matches. Glenn Roeder would come in and steady the ship with a tremendous end to a tumultuous season but that’s a story for another day. Newcastle 1-0 Arsenal.

Industry observers note that malcolm Macdonald – Some of our older readers will have fond memories of this legendary number nine. ‘Supermac’, as he was affectionately known by fans, kick-started his Toon career with a hat-trick in his first home match against Liverpool. What was to follow has gone down in Toon Army folklore! Scoring one hundred and twenty-one goals in just two hundred and twenty-seven appearances has him up there with the best of the best in NUFC history. Perhaps his finest hour came in the 1974 FA Cup Semi-Final when he scored two second half goals to defeat Burnley 2-0 at Hillsborough and send United to their first FA Cup final for nineteen years. Unfortunately, he couldn’t repeat this feat at Wembley as a tame performance was punished by a 3-0 defeat to a Kevin Keegan inspired Liverpool. There was uproar when he was sold to Arsenal for a third of a million pounds in 1976. He went on to score forty-two goals in eighty-four league games for the Gunners.

Industry observers note that andy Cole began his career by playing one league game for Arsenal before being loaned to Fulham and then sold to Bristol City. Kevin Keegan broke the club’s transfer record by splashing out £1.75 million for the striker in 1993. This is a number nine who’s record stands up to anyone else’s – a whopping sixty-eight goals in eighty-four matches before being controversially sold to Man United in January 1995 for a British record transfer fee. Some fans were so angry at the sale that they turned up at the stadium demanding answers which Keegan provided, famously standing on the steps to explain his decision. King Kev would go on to sign both Sir Les and Alan Shearer as the entertainers came ‘so close’ to being champions of England for the first time since 1927 and the debate still rages on about which of the three was the best number nine of NUFC’s Premier League era.

It has been revealed that sol Campbell was something of a legend at Arsenal having run down his contract at arch-rivals Tottenham to join the Gunners on a free transfer. He’d go on to win a number of trophies and even grabbed a goal in the 2006 Champions League final. He played a handful of games for NUFC in 2010 but it’s safe to say he was well past his best when donning the famous black and white.

In a recent development, matthias Jaissle after a 1-1 draw away at Fulham: “A step in the right direction after the last performance. That’s something we can really build on.I think there were occasions also to win that game. Of course, the disallowed goal, a soft one, I would say. I see it differently then also a big chance at the end. Then you should go home with three points but one point and a performance is something we can work on. It’s now time to reflect and recharge also with a long season ahead of us, then pull out the things we need to improve and there are a couple of aspects, but today showed a clear direction in the right way so we can build on that. We did enough to win. We spoke clearly through the week and we saw that today, there was complete commitment and togetherness in all phases. The first 20 minutes there was a lack of confidence from last week but we grew through the game and that was excellent, something to build on.”.

Mikel Arteta after a 1-0 win at home to Hull City:  “Not beautiful but effective. I’m delighted with the win because to go to the international break after winning is one of the best things for a coach or for a player. I think, regarding the performance, we were the better team. I think we had enough chances and situations to make the scoreline much bigger. We weren’t efficient enough to do that, and then we have to rely on generating volume, generating a lot of situations in and around the box until we are able to break them down.This is exactly how we won the game, and Martin, the way he scores, is not the most beautiful one but the most effective one, which is a simple shot and then following the next action, and that was enough today to win again.”.

Newcastle United fans food bank will once again be collecting opposite the Gallowgate end and gratefully receiving food, money and toiletries for those in need. Of particular interest are non-perishable food and drink items (such as noodles, pasta, rice, canned food, soup, cereal, cordial, long life milk etc) as well as toiletries such as shower gel, shampoo, toothpaste and sanitary products. Please give whatever you can, any donation is very much appreciated.

For further info and/or to donate online go to Newcastle Foodbank.

There can be no doubt that Newcastle have been poor recently despite showing some promising signs of improvement against Fulham last match. Games after an international break are notoriously difficult to predict. The bookies may be looking at this as something of a formality but we seem to do a lot better against the bigger sides and have a great recent record at home against the Gunners. I was thinking this may be a score draw but my confidence has been growing throughout the week so I’m going for a wildly-celebrated win followed by a few sore heads on Sunday morning. Newcastle 2-1 Arsenal.

Aston Villa’s tour of the Far East ended in defeat as they lost 2-1 to German champions Bayern Munich in a pre-season friendly at the Kai Tak Sports Park in Hong Kong on Friday.

Industry observers note that bayern took the lead inside the final 10 minutes of the first half, with defender Kim Min-jae heading in from Tom Bischof’s sublime free-kick. Villa goalkeeper Marco Bizot made a string of saves in the second half to keep Bayern’s lead at one goal until former Liverpool forward Luis Díaz smashed in Bayern’s second off the underside of the bar.

Just as the game appeared to be out of reach for Aston Villa, who had struggled to create much going forward for most of the game, Unai Emery’s side highlighted some life late on. Summer signing João Gomes’s goal from the edge of the box gave them hope before Tammy Abraham nearly brought them back onto level terms, only to be denied by a fine save from 40-year-old Manuel Neuer.

Aston Villa are next in action in six days’ time when they take on Paris St-Germain in the Uefa Super Cup before kicking off their Premier League campaign at Brighton. Bayern have one more friendly to come against RB Leipzig before the DFL-Supercup against Borussia Dortmund. They then kick off the defence of their Bundesliga crown against Stuttgart at home on August 28.

In a recent development, stepping up in the big moments! 🐐🧤 pic.twitter.com/r14rF39XpR.

Unai Emery’s men head home from the Far East to face PSG in the Uefa Super Cup in Salzburg next week and then have one more pre-season friendly against Borussia Monchengladbach before starting their Premier League campaign at Brighton.

Bizot nearly has a calamitous moment coming out of his penalty area but gets away with it.

It has been revealed that the final whistle is blown soon after and Bayern hold on to beat Villa 2-1 in Hong Kong. They had looked comfortable when Diaz put them 2-0 up but Villa kept going until the end.

The space opens up for Palhinha to shoot from range but Bizot makes a fairly comfortable save down to his right.

It was all Bayern for 80 minutes of this game but Villa have come to life in the closing stages, with Vincent Kompany’s side now holding on a bit.

There will be four added minutes.

Industry observers note that when Diaz scored Bayern’s second goal, Aston Villa were out of this game but it has been all Villa since then. They look the more likely to get a goal.

Gomes’ free-kick out on the left is parried behind by Neuer for a Villa corner on the right. The corner comes to nothing.

For 80 minutes, Aston Villa barely looked like scoring but come so close to getting two goals in just a few minutes. Abraham meets a cross from the right and must think he has scored but his header is brilliantly saved by the 40-year-old Neuer.

Maybe this game is not quite done and dusted yet. A cross from the right picks out Gomes on the edge of the box. The Brazilian takes one touch before toe poking past Neuer and into the Bayern net. Gomes meant that finish and Villa have some hope.

According to recent reports, abraham should have done better there. He has the space to drive down Villa’s right and has a decision to make; cross the ball to his left and drive forward himself to shoot. He takes a while to make the decision before his attempted cross is intercepted by Ito.

Boey’s yellow card was his final act of the game as he is replaced by Della Rovere. Boey did seem to be struggling with some cramp.

Bayern receive their second yellow card of the game as Boey is booked for cynically pulling down Lynch.

Cash, Maatsen and Buendia have gone off for Aston Villa.

Double substitution from Bayern as Pavic and Assomo replace Tah and Brown.

According to recent reports, A fantastic goal to put the Germans 2-0 up and it is nothing more than they deserve. Ibrahimovic finds Diaz in space on the left and the Colombian drives at Cash. As he enters the Villa box, Diaz cuts inside onto his preferred right foot and smashes a shot towards goal. It appeared to go right over Bizot, who opts not to put a hand up. The ball crashes off the underside of the bar and goes in. It has been all Bayern in this second half and that goal had been coming.

Industry observers note that bayern are knocking on the door and come very close to doubling their lead. Diaz’s shot from the edge of the box looks destined to hit the net with Bizot beaten but fortunately for Villa Abraham is on hand on his own goal line to make the block.

It has been revealed that bizot makes another great save. Bayern win a free-kick out on the right after Brown was fouled. Bischoff opts to shoot instead of crossing and nearly beats Bizot at his near post but the Aston Villa keeper gets across to his left to make the save.

According to recent reports, unai Emery makes a double substitution as Mings and Lynch replace Torres and Guessand. Mings takes the captain’s armband.

That is a fantastic double save from Bizot, first denying Stanisic and then Ibrahimovic. Both of those shots came through bodies so Bizot did a good job of reacting and making the saves with his legs on both occasions.

It is safe to say the Bayern fans out in Hong Kong love Diaz, who is cheered every time he touches the ball.

Vincent Kompany is going to make a triple change as Ito, Diaz and Palhinha come on. Former Liverpool man Diaz received a great ovation from the fans in Hong Kong. Palhinha, who spent last season on loan at Tottenha, has been linked with a move to Aston Villa in this window.

In a recent development, should Bayern have been awarded a penalty there? A ball is played in behind the Villa defence into the penalty area and Ibrahimovic appeared to be brought down but the referee waves those appeals away. On first viewing, that appeared to be a penalty.

Just before the hour mark, it is time for some changes from Aston Villa. Abraham and Bogarde come on for Madjo and Kamara. This is Abraham’s first appearance of this pre-season.

Good play from Gomes earns Aston Villa a free-kick not far outside the Bayern penalty area out on the left, in a similar position to the free-kick that Bayern scored from in the first half. Buendia clips in a good ball to the back post, where Guessand looks likely to score but instead misses the ball on the stretch. Should Guessand have done better with that? Probably.

Brown was starting in his customary left-back position for Bayern in the first half but is now operating out on the right wing.

Gomes leaves one late on Pavlovic and, had this been a competitive fixture, I suspect that might have been a yellow card.

According to recent reports, aston Villa have struggled to create much going forward and have not really had a genuine goal-scoring opportunity in this first half. Their forward line though will look quite different when they kick off the seaosn than it does today.

In a recent development, the German side take the lead in Hong Kong. Bischof’s left-footed delivery from a free-kick out on the left is sublime, whipping it right into the corridor of uncertainty. The quality of delivery means it is quite a simple header for Kim, who makes no mistake with his header into the far corner. Kim might have been offside but obviously there is no VAR in use today. 1-0 Bayern.

Sources indicate that that is a waste in the end from Bayern. Boey fires a pass in-field into Laimer, who takes a fantastic first touch on the turn inside the Villa half. He drives through the Villa half and at the penalty area but his pass outside looking for Cardozo is poor and overhit, with the ball rolling out for a goal kick. Laimer will be annoyed at himself having done all the hard work and then failed to execute the easy part.

It has been revealed that bischof eyes one up from range and tries to pick out the top corner. Bizot is routed to his spot and is hoping the shot goes wide. Bischof’s effort is always curling wide, much to Bizot’s relief.

It has been revealed that the first booking of the game goes the way of Bayern Munich. Guessand drives forward into the Bayern half and is brought down by a cynical foul from Cardozo. You were half expecting Cardozo to perhaps escape without a booking with it being a pre-season friendly but he does not. It was the right call to book him.

According to recent reports, bayern force Villa into an error and win themselves a corner as a result out on the left. It is delivered into a dangerous area at the front post but Villa do a good job of handling it and clearing their lines.

Bayern Munich have made two signings this summer; Brown from Bundesliga rivals Frankfurt and Saibari from PSV. Brown feels like such a Bayern signing, nabbing a good player from a Bundesliga rival.

Sources indicate that aston Villa have made four signings so far this summer but just one is in their starting XI today in the form of Gomes, who joined from Midlands rivals Wolves this summer. Young Swiss midfielder Manzambi has joined from Freiburg but is at the moment out injured. Garnacho picked up a knock and Cisse, who has arrived from LASK, is not involved for Villa today.

It has been revealed that the ball is played in behind the Aston Villa defence to pick out the run of Binder. On the edge of the Villa box, Binder gets the first touch but Lindelof is calm in defence and heads back to his keeper Bizot.

Moments later, Gomes is dispossessed inside his own half and Ibrahimovic has a shot from just outside the box but drags it wide of the far post.

According to recent reports, good work from 17-year-old Madjo down Aston Villa’s left wins them their first corner of the game. Buendia’s inswinger is headed away too easily at the near post. Aston Villa have seen their former set-piece coach Austin MacPhee nabbed this summer by Xabi Alonso’s Chelsea.

The referee is allowing the game to flow and thus not blowing for soft fouls.

Industry observers note that the first chance of the game falls to Bayern Munich. Brown’s cross from the left is headed by Maatsen straight to Ibrahimovic on the edge of the box. Ibrahimovic, not any relation to Zlatan, takes the shot on first time but it is blocked by Maatsen, who makes up for that poor header with the block. The ball goes behind for a corner, which comes to nothing.

Interestingly, there are only eight outfield substitutions on the Aston Villa bench for this game, with the likes of Garnacho and McGinn picking up knocks the other day. It appears then that at least a couple of Villa outfield players will have to play the full 90.

Both sides emerge from the tunnel, Aston Villa led out by Matty Cash and Bayern Munich by Manuel Neuer, and we are closing in on kick-off in Hong Kong. A group of delegates shake the hands of both starting XIs.

Chelsea and Juventus played in this stadium the other night and it is safe to say that the pitch does not look in the best state ahead of kick-off today. It looks like it will continue to rip up and the last thing the two managers will want is to pick up any serious injuries.

Currently, before the two sides emerge, the crowd in Hong Kong are being treated to some pre-match dancing and entertainment, which includes people dressed as pandas and sharks dancing. Would the Premier League ever take inspiration and have dancing pandas before kick-off?

It has been a big summer of change at Aston Villa already and there could be more changes before the end of the window. Industry observers note that “Aston Villa are a top side with a very good coach. They have a large squad and will field plenty of talent. They have already played more friendlies than us, but for us it is a good challenge. It is a match in which we will learn a lot about our team’s fitness. It will be a good match for us.”.

Sources indicate that “It is difficult to improve; after all, it is not just about the trophies we have won, but also about the number of goals and matches we have won. It is possible, but difficult. Aston Villa’s preparations for the new season continue out in Hong Kong as they take on Bundesliga champions Bayern Munich at the Kai Tak Stadium. These sides have met twice before; Aston Villa beat Bayern 1-0 to win the European Cup in 1981/82 before then meeting in the Champions League group stages during the 2024/25 season, with Jhon Duran’s long-range screamer giving Aston Villa a 1-0 win at Villa Park.

After losing two of their first three pre-season friendlies, Aston Villa have won their first two games on Asian soil and this game marks the end of their tour of the Far East. It has been a summer of significant change at Aston Villa thus far with some key members of their squad departing and some new faces arriving. Youri Tielemans has departed after Manchester United triggered his release clause and they then sold Morgan Rogers to Chelsea for a British transfer record £117m. Unai Emery’s side have brought in 20-year-old Swiss midfielder Johan Manzambi, Brazilian midfielder Joao Gomes and Alejandro Garnacho, with the deal for Garnacho being an initial loan. Manzambi is currently on the sidelines due to a knee injury.

Unai Emery’s side were dealt a blow during the World Cup as Belgian midfielder Amadou Onana picked up a serious knee injury. They were though boosted by the return of Boubacar Kamara after seven months out as he scored in the 3-1 friendly victory over BG Parthum. As one midfielder returned from injury in that game, another picked up a fresh injury as John McGinn suffered a knock to his knee. The likes of Ollie Watkins, Ezri Konsa and Emi Martinez are yet to return after their world Cup exploits. They begin their Premier League campaign with an away game on the south coast against Brighton on August 23 but will be involved in the Uefa Super Cup against PSG next week having lifted the Europa League last season.

According to recent reports, bayern Munich head into this season looking to win a third straight Bundesliga title and have won two of their three friendlies, losing once. They have added Moroccan attacker Ismael Saibari from PSV and German left-back Nathaniel Brown from Bundesliga rivals Eintracht Frankfurt to their ranks this summer. The likes of Harry Kane, Dayot Upamecano and Michael Olise are not available as they are still yet to return after World Cup duty but Vincent Kompany has confirmed that Bayern’s German stars are set to return.

After today, Bayern have one more friendly against RB Leipzig before the DFL-Supercup against Borussia Dortmund. They then kick off the defence of their Bundesliga crown against Stuttgart at home on August 28.

I’m going back to last (2025-26) season and comparing it with this 2026-27 season after 10 games.

The difference in the Premier League table between now and last season after 10 games. The difference? One place higher than last season, from 13th to 12th.

It had me wondering, is it going to be such a season again?

In a recent development, these next four matches could be pivotal when it comes to the morale of the players and whether we fall into a relegation battle, maybe even the future of Matthias Jaissle at St. James’ Park will be at risk.

What this season is going to bring is still a mystery but the early signs don’t look promising….

By Axel Clody | 20 Nov 2026 06:29.

In a recent development, lucas Chevalier wants to leave Paris Saint-Germain in the next winter transfer window. The Parisian club are ready to let him go on one condition.

Having joined PSG in the summer of 2025 from Lille for £34m (€40m), Lucas Chevalier has failed to make his mark at the Parisian club. While he was expected to succeed Gianluigi Donnarumma, he now finds himself as a mere understudy to Matvey Safonov.

The Russian goalkeeper has won his place as first choice and is not letting go of it. Paris are very pleased with his performances and have reportedly even secretly wrapped up a contract extension. Safonov has played every game for the two-time European champions this season, leaving Lucas Chevalier without any game time.

It is a difficult situation for the French international, who missed the last World Cup and has not been called up by upcoming France manager Zinedine Zidane.

Sources indicate that already mentioned as a possible departure last summer, the former Lille man had chosen to stay. Canal+ reports that PSG had told him he would get a fresh chance if he kept working.

In a recent development, however, that chance never came. A point of no return appears to have been reached. ‘He wants to play, he needs to play. Today, his wish is to look elsewhere to find game time’ - Gauthier Kuntzmann revealed on the Late Football Club show. The Parisian club are ready to let him leave this winter.

It has been revealed that ‘Paris Saint-Germain are aware that the situation of Lucas Chevalier cannot drag on. On top of that, he is losing market value and that is a factor, even if everything is going very well financially at PSG. 'I am telling you, Paris Saint-Germain do not rule out the idea, even in the short term, of seeing Lucas Chevalier leave on loan or in a sale, it will depend on the offers’ - Philippe Carayon explained on the same show.

Recent findings suggest that the task does not look simple for Lucas Chevalier. ‘Finding a goalkeeper position at a good club in January will not be simple. Except in the event of an injury at a club’ - Alain Roche warned. In any case, in this saga, PSG will only let their goalkeeper leave on one condition.

According to recent reports, ‘There will be an absolute prerequisite for Paris Saint-Germain, which is to find a top-level replacement for Safonov’ - Philippe Carayon stressed. That could complicate a departure for the French goalkeeper in January 2027 even further.

Chelsea cruised to victory over Ruben Amorim’s AC Milan in Jakarta, Indonesia, on Saturday. Goals from Moises Caicedo and a double from João Pedro either side of half-time led Xabi Alonso’s side to their second win on their Far East tour.

The game was fairly even in the first half and looked set to head into the break level at 0-0 but Pedro’s header from Moises Caicedo’s corner put Chelsea in front.

The west London side then doubled their advantage seconds into the second half as Pedro scored his second, assisted by Pedro Neto.

Sources indicate that just minutes later, Chelsea had their third courtesy of a well-worked corner routine. Romeo Lavia’s delivery was met by Caicedo on the volley, with the Ecuadorian’s finish with the outside of the boot finding the bottom corner.

Chelsea conclude their tour of the Far East with a game against Johor Darul Ta’zim on Sunday in Malaysia before returning home.

Their final pre-season game will be against Real Sociedad at Stamford Bridge before beginning their Premier League campaign at Fulham.

AC Milan take on Amorim’s former club Manchester United next Saturday before they kick off their Serie A campaign at Torino on August 23.

He is among the new breed of coaches who are rock stars in their own right, taking centre-stage since rules were changed so that only one person is allowed in the technical area at a time. For MacPhee to get closer to the players for a set-piece, it will mean Xabi Alonso taking a step back onto the bench.

It has been an incredible rise for MacPhee, 46, who was working on Michael O’Neill’s staff with Northern Ireland 10 years ago this summer, helping them reach the knockout stages of the European Championship.

Industry observers note that chelsea take on Johor Darul Ta’zim in Malaysia tomorrow before returning to the UK. Their final pre-season game will be against Real Sociedad before taking on Fulham on the opening weekend of the new season.

The teams emerge from the tunnel and we are just moments away from kick-off in Indonesia.

Recent findings suggest that the trophies won by Franco Baresi, who has died at the age of 66, are their own monument to the AC Milan and Italy defender’s greatness. Six times a Serie A champion, five as captain, three European Cup-winning campaigns, 10 other winners’ medals and the distinction of being a member of Italy squads that finished in first, second and third places at World Cup tournaments demonstrate that his career, in a significantly more meritocratic era, stand alongside the giants even if the bias towards attacking virtuosos denied him the Ballon d’Or his talent deserved.

In a recent development, yet they do not tell us why the grief, so tangible in Milan and beyond today, transcends tribal rivalry. It would be unfair to say that he transformed the art of Italian defending. Gaetano Scirea, the elegant Juventus sweeper who kept the 21-year-old Baresi confined to the bench when Italy won their third World Cup in 1982, had a surplus of natural ability, composure and intelligence. He did not need the raw-elbowed brutality of Claudio Gentile, heir to generations of Italian defenders influenced by the post-war influx of players brought up in the traditions of Argentina and Uruguay.

Chelsea’s pre-season continues out in the Far East as they take on AC Milan in the Gelora Bung Karno Stadium in Jakarta, Indonesia. Both clubs now have new managers, with Xabi Alonso taking over at Chelsea and former Manchester United boss Ruben Amorim now at the helm at AC Milan. These sides met in pre-season last year, with Chelsea winning 4-1 at Stamford Bridge. At that time, now-Manchester City boss Enzo Maresca was in charge whilst Max Allegri, who is now at Napoli, was leading AC Milan. The last time they met competitively was during the 2022/23 Champions League season, with Chelsea winning both games.

Chelsea lost 1-0 to AC Milan’s Serie A rivals Juventus on Wednesday in Hong Kong, in which Danny Welbeck made his first Chelsea appearance after joining from Brighton in the last week.

“We want to have a great team spirit and that is built on a daily basis with a great culture in the building,” Alonso said in his pre-match press conference. “That helps in the moment you have to compete. You feel better having that togetherness, trust, and the bonds between the players are so important to ultimately building a winning mentality, and a team that can compete anywhere. So the football side is so important, but the mental side is as important. And the strength of the team is the most important. We have been able to train and prepare [during pre-season] and I am very happy with the attitude and personality, we know that it is a very important part of this tour.”.

It has been revealed that it has been another busy week on the transfer front for Chelsea; not only has Welbeck arrived over the last week but so too have Jordan Henderson and Valentin Barco. Alonso’s men have two more games after this against Johor Darul Ta’zim and Real Sociedad before getting their Premier League campaign under way with a derby against Fulham at Craven Cottage.

In a recent development, AC Milan finished fifth in Serie A last season to earn a spot in the Europa League last season. Their massive-money acquisition this summer as been Portuguese striker Goncalo Ramos from PSG. They have played two pre-season friendlies so far, which have both ended in draws; 2-2 against Celtic and then 1-1 against city rivals Inter. They kick off their Serie A campaign at Torino on August 23.

Tropical land-use intensification restructures biodiversity

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 69 min read (13722 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

⏱️ ~69 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that tropical land-use intensification threatens global biodiversity, yet most assessments of tropical agricultural landscapes focus on local-scale biodiversity, overlooking how land use restructures biodiversity across space and multiple taxa.
  • Across many tropical regions, biodiverse old-growth rainforests have been replaced by tree-cash-crop monocultures, including oil palm, rubber, coffee, cacao and timber plantations5.
  • It has been revealed that the multiple negative effects of land-use change and intensification on tropical biodiversity are increasingly well documented, particularly at the local scale (α-diversity).
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that tropical land-use intensification threatens global biodiversity, yet most assessments of tropical agricultural landscapes focus on local-scale biodiversity, overlooking how land use restructures biodiversity across space and multiple taxa. Here we provide an ecosystem-wide assessment of 24 taxonomic groups across all domains of life—encompassing 40,049 species—along a land-use intensification gradient from lowland forests to intensively managed smallholder cash-crop monocultures in Indonesian landscapes. Despite widespread losses of landscape and local multidiversity1 in monocultures (approximately 78% and 50%, respectively), we found no evidence for consistent community homogenization with land-use intensification. Instead, monocultures exhibit a systematic shift from turnover to nestedness for aboveground taxa. Such patterns of differentiation may mask trajectories towards biotic homogenization via early stages of assemblage simplification. Biotic differentiation has the potential to partly mitigate biodiversity losses by positively affecting γ-diversity. This opens management options, including the conservation of existing remnants of traditional agriculture and the implementation of sustainable management practices2,3,4. Our results demonstrate that tropical land-use intensification restructures biodiversity not only through species loss, but also via a pervasive reorganization of community composition across trophic levels. Conserving tropical biodiversity, therefore, requires a multi-taxon, landscape-scale perspective that explicitly integrates agricultural land uses with the protection of natural and semi-natural habitats to reconcile agricultural production and conservation.

Across many tropical regions, biodiverse old-growth rainforests have been replaced by tree-cash-crop monocultures, including oil palm, rubber, coffee, cacao and timber plantations5. At the same time, both traditional and modern tropical agroforestry systems6—long regarded as reconciling production with ecological sustainability—are being displaced by more intensive agriculture7,8. Such trends in land-use change and land-use intensification pose a substantial threat to the biodiversity and functioning of tropical ecosystems9,10. Quantifying their effects, however, remains challenging owing to the vast effort required to conduct multitrophic inventories of hyperdiverse tropical ecosystems, the often contrasting responses of different taxa, and the scale-dependence of biodiversity11.

It has been revealed that the multiple negative effects of land-use change and intensification on tropical biodiversity are increasingly well documented, particularly at the local scale (α-diversity). Previous investigations have shown that α-diversity in tropical agricultural systems is typically substantially lower than in forests, with diminished species diversity linked to declines in ecological functions12,13,14,15. Although protected areas are central to mitigating these negative effects16, the long-term persistence of tropical biodiversity will also depend on conservation beyond reserve boundaries. Designing biodiversity-friendly tropical agricultural mosaic landscapes that sustain regional diversity (γ-diversity) without compromising economic objectives is therefore critical3,8,15. Achieving this goal requires a thorough understanding of how community composition varies among sites (β-diversity)17. β-Diversity arises either from species replacement among sites, with each site hosting a different set of species (turnover), or from species-poorer communities forming subsets of species-richer ones (nestedness)18. Identifying the spatial, environmental and management-related drivers of β-diversity in the context of land-use intensification in hyperdiverse tropical ecosystems may thus guide more effective landscape-scale management19.

An important yet understudied process in this context is biotic homogenization, which has been suggested to be the dominant dynamic shaping species communities and global biodiversity in the Anthropocene20. Biotic homogenization occurs when communities become increasingly similar in composition, often through the loss of specialized, rare or forest-dependent species and their replacement by widespread generalists, including non-native species21. By contrast, biotic differentiation occurs when communities become more dissimilar in species composition, arising from local gains, such as the introduction of non-natives, or from species losses, including the extinction of dominant native species17,22. Patterns of species losses and gains can mask the progressive erosion of biota in formerly forested landscapes, thereby obscuring the true magnitude of the global biodiversity crisis. In heterogeneous agricultural landscapes, differentiation can also result from a variety of semi-natural habitats that support distinct species assemblages. Because homogenization and differentiation can occur simultaneously, understanding their combined dynamics is essential for assessing the full impact of land-use intensification—yet this interplay remains insufficiently explored17,22.

Here we fill this knowledge gap through systematic biodiversity inventories of 24 taxonomic groups across all domains of life, multiple trophic levels, and both aboveground and belowground compartments. Communities were sampled across four different land uses—lowland forests, and three agricultural land uses: low-intensity rubber agroforests (hereafter referred to as jungle rubber) and intensively managed smallholder rubber and oil palm plantations (Fig. 1). Biodiversity and environmental data were collected using a standardized design across 32 sampling plots distributed across 2 distinct landscapes within the smallholder-dominated agricultural tropical lowlands of Jambi Province in Sumatra, Indonesia (Extended Data Fig. 1). This comprehensive dataset builds on a long-term collaborative research programme that has generated detailed taxonomic, functional and trophic information, as well as integrative analyses that link ecological and socio-economic dimensions (Methods). Leveraging this foundation, we provide a novel perspective by investigating the effects of tropical land-use intensification on multitrophic community assemblages at multiple spatial scales. Indonesia combines exceptional biodiversity with one of the world’s highest rates of deforestation, making it a critical frontier of tropical land-use change23,24,25 and a model region for studying land-use trajectories that are increasingly characteristic of smallholder-dominated tropical regions globally.

We find that the few remaining tropical forests in the region constitute irreplaceable reservoirs of biodiversity. Overall, 5,861 species occurred exclusively in forest (15% of all recorded species in our study; including species, morphospecies and operational taxonomic units (OTUs) or amplicon sequence variants—hereafter referred to as species), including 1,510 aboveground species (30% of all aboveground species) and 4,351 belowground species (12% of all belowground species) (Fig. 1). Forest-dependence was most pronounced for trees, understorey plants and mesostigmatid mites, each with at least 40% of strictly forest-associated species (Extended Data Figs. 2 and 3). These estimates are conservative because our sampling design included three times more agricultural plots than forest plots (Supplementary Figs. 1–3), whereas our sampling effort was equal across all four land-use types. Furthermore, the remaining forests in our study landscapes have faced degradation. Thus, the data probably underestimate the biodiversity potential of intact forests and instead reflect the current trajectory of forest degradation26. Together, these results indicate that a significant proportion of the species pool depends on forests, underscoring the urgency of restoring remaining forest habitats while conserving and preventing further agricultural expansion16,27 and ongoing forest degradation28.

According to recent reports, A substantial fraction of biodiversity persisted in agricultural smallholder landscapes: nearly 40% of the recorded species can be considered as forest generalists—that is, species found in both forest and one or more agricultural land uses (15,889 species, 1,966 aboveground and 13,923 belowground taxa). However, almost half of the forest aboveground generalist species (1,966 species) were absent from monocultures and occurred only in forest and jungle rubber (823 species; Fig. 1). At least 60% of aboveground biodiversity (3,057 species) was confined to forest and jungle rubber, and was thus vulnerable to the ongoing loss of (agro)forests13. This trend was especially pronounced for canopy bugs (Hemiptera), hymenopteran parasitoids, spiders and trees (more than 20% of their species were shared only between these two land uses) and bats (40% was shared between these two land uses; Extended Data Fig. 2). Of all belowground species, 19% (6,481 species) were shared across all land uses, with 7% of the species only shared between forest and jungle rubber (2,542 species; Extended Data Fig. 3). The substantial overlap between aboveground forest and jungle rubber communities provides strong empirical evidence that agroforests offer a suitable habitat for a considerably higher number of forest-dependent species than monocultures29,30. Although agroforests cannot replace intact forests, the biodiversity value of traditional agricultural systems, which buffer biodiversity losses in this agricultural landscape, should be recognized. Agroforests also represent a potential leverage point for enhancing biodiversity in human-modified landscapes28, for example, by enriching existing monocultures with native trees3,4.

Industry observers note that overall, land-use intensification drove a marked shift from a species-rich pool of aboveground forest-dependent species to a smaller set of species associated with monocultures. This transition was accompanied by pronounced losses in γ-multidiversity—defined as the average of standardized species richness values across taxonomic groups1 within each land use. Relative to forest (γ-multidiversity = 0.91), γ-multidiversity decreased by 20% in jungle rubber (0.73) and by around 78% in monocultures (0.20) (Fig. 2; Extended Data Fig. 4 for aboveground and belowground γ-multidiversity separately). Thus, our results show clear biodiversity losses with intensification, especially for aboveground species.

Linear model fits using ggeffect (marginal mean and 95% confidence intervals, n = 32 plots). Letters indicate statistically significant pairwise differences (P < 0.05) based on multiple comparisons of means using Tukey’s contrast, with P values adjusted for the false discovery rate. b, Points and lines (mean and 95% confidence intervals using 10,000 bootstrap replicates) represent log ratio in diversity associated with land-use intensification using forests as a control. Confidence intervals not overlapping zero indicate differences from the forest (coloured points; black confidence intervals; paler colours indicate when the 95% confidence intervals include zero). Negative and positive values indicate decreases (loss of species richness or homogenization) or gains in species richness and differentiation when compared to mean forest values, respectively. For β-multidiversity components, negative and positive values similarly represent decreases or increases in turnover or nestedness relative to forest turnover and nestedness; values for single taxonomic groups are shown in Extended Data Fig. 6.

According to recent reports, we hypothesized that land-use intensification would consistently reduce α-diversity across taxa and promote biotic homogenization, such that an agricultural land-use type would harbour more similar communities (lower β-diversity) than forests. By contrast, biotic differentiation occurs when communities become more dissimilar in species composition under an agricultural land use than in forests. To test this hypothesis, we quantified α-diversity as local species richness and α-multidiversity. The α-multidiversity is defined as the average of standardized species richness across taxonomic groups at the plot level1 for each land use using the min–max scaling approach (Methods). To assess changes in community composition within each land use, we quantified β-diversity as aggregated pairwise dissimilarities per plot, and β-multidiversity as the average standardized β-diversity across taxonomic groups per plot using the min–max scaling approach.

Industry observers note that we observed a substantial decline in α-multidiversity with land-use intensification (R2 = 0.81, F = 38.68; P < 0.001; Fig. 2, Extended Data Table 1 and Extended Data Figs. 4 and 5), decreasing from 0.59 in forest (95% confidence interval: 0.54–0.65) to 0.47 in jungle rubber (95% confidence interval: 0.42–0.52) and 0.26 and 0.28 in rubber and oil palm plantations, respectively (95% confidence intervals: 0.21–0.32 and 0.23–0.34, respectively; Fig. 2 and Extended Data Table 1). This corresponds to an approximately 50% loss of α-multidiversity from forest to monocultures (Fig. 2). Significant declines relative to forest were observed in 15, 21 and 21 taxonomic groups in jungle rubber, rubber and oil palm plantations, respectively, corresponding to 75%, 94%, and 100% of aboveground taxa, and 38%, 75%, and 63% of belowground taxa (Fig. 2). Trees exhibited the strongest shifts, as they are directly affected by deforestation, planting, and current management practices (herbicide application, manual weeding, liming and fertilizer use), as well as by altered microclimatic and soil-related site conditions in plantations13,30. Such biodiversity losses in monocultures may be partly mitigated locally by improved management31 and diversified, sustainable production systems3,4.

Soil bacteria across agricultural land uses and archaea in oil palm plantations were the only groups in which significant species gains relative to forests were observed (Fig. 2). Species gains for these groups can emerge, for example, as a result of management practices such as liming and fertilization, which increase the soil pH32 and the availability of bio-available nitrogen improving growth conditions for specific bacterial and archaeal taxa33. However, these groups show pronounced shifts in community composition and biotic homogenization (details below; Fig. 2 and Supplementary Fig. 4), highlighting that changes in species richness alone cannot capture the ecosystem-wide effects of land-use intensification.

β-Multidiversity showed only subtle, yet significant, changes across land uses (based on standardized Jaccard; R2 = 0.30, F = 4.06, P = 0.016; Fig. 2 and Extended Data Table 2). This less pronounced multidiversity loss was partly explained by taxon-specific patterns of biotic homogenization or differentiation (Fig. 2). Significant biotic homogenization—lower β-diversity in the agricultural land uses relative to β-diversity in forests—was found in 5, 6 and 9 taxonomic groups in jungle rubber, rubber and oil palm, respectively; whereas 9, 13 and 12 groups showed significant differentiation—higher β-diversity in the agricultural land uses relative to forests. The remaining groups showed neither significant homogenization nor differentiation. Only 10 out of 24 taxonomic groups responded consistently across agricultural systems—either homogenization (understorey plants, fungi and bacteria) or differentiation (canopy bugs, flies, parasitoids, spiders, butterflies, leaf litter beetles and oribatid mites; Fig. 2).

Sources indicate that idiosyncratic responses probably reflect land-use-specific effects on habitats and the interactions between disturbance and environmental heterogeneity19,34 (Supplementary Fig. 5). For example, biotic and abiotic filtering may drive homogenization in tree communities by directly causing the loss of forest specialists through management. Effects can also act indirectly via resource homogenization—for example, through fertilization or homogenization of plant resources in terms of composition and seasonality, impacting niche segregation across trophic and non-trophic interactions. Further indirect effects act via seed dispersal, recruitment, growth and survival34. Similarly, homogenization in soil microbial communities may arise from filtering through shifts in plant–fungal associations35 and from reduced dispersal limitation via passive dispersal36,37,38. By contrast, biotic differentiation can arise from spillover and occasional species, as observed previously in arthropods19 and supported by our results on abundance-based dissimilarity indices for canopy arthropods (Supplementary Results). Biotic homogenization and differentiation can result not only from changes in community composition but also from changes in spatial aggregation, species abundance distributions and individual densities per unit area39. These ecological mechanisms are biologically relevant, modified by land-use intensification and captured by our approach39.

Sources indicate that turnover was the dominant component of β-multidiversity across land uses, ranging from zero in oil palm for trees to 0.93 in rubber for leaf litter spiders. Turnover multidiversity reflects the extent to which sites within the same land use host distinct species assemblages across multiple taxonomic groups. Turnover multidiversity increased in jungle rubber (log ratio: 0.07; 95% confidence interval: 0.02 to 0.11) and decreased in monocultures (log ratio rubber: −0.10; 95% confidence interval: −0.15 to −0.06 and log ratio oil palm: −0.09; 95% confidence interval: −0.13 to −0.05) compared with forest (Fig. 2). Stronger declines in turnover multidiversity were observed in oil palm for aboveground taxa (log ratio: −0.10; 95% confidence interval: −0.15 to −0.07) and in rubber for belowground taxa (log ratio: −0.30; 95% confidence interval: −0.44 to −0.22; Extended Data Fig. 6). Nestedness across land uses ranged from 0.02 in jungle rubber for fungi to 0.48 in rubber for centipedes. Relative to forest, nestedness multidiversity—indicating assemblages in species-poor sites forming subsets of those in species-rich sites within the same land use across taxonomic groups—increased for aboveground taxa in rubber (log ratio: 0.38; 95% confidence interval: 0.27–0.47) and oil palm (log ratio: 0.32; 95% confidence interval: 0.23–0.44) plantations and decreased on belowground taxa in jungle rubber (log ratio: −0.44; 95% confidence interval: −0.58 to −0.28) and oil palm (log ratio: −0.40; 95% confidence interval: −0.52 to −0.18) plantations (Fig. 2 and Extended Data Fig. 6).

Our results reveal that disentangling the components underlying biotic differentiation within each land use is essential; differentiation emerging from nested assemblages has different implications for conservation and landscape management than differentiation emerging from the uniqueness of species assemblages. Distinguishing these processes sharpens our ability to anticipate trajectories of biotic homogenization, including the delayed effects of extinction debt and colonization lags, whereby an apparent differentiation may in fact reflect assemblage simplification before a transition towards homogenization occurs17,19,22. Biotic differentiation can emerge when differences—for example, in local landscape properties—among sites lead to increasing differentiation over time, resulting in homogenization within the same landscape but differentiation among landscapes (landscape divergence hypothesis)40. Weak homogenization or biotic differentiation can also result from higher forest cover in smallholder landscapes; forest cover may guard against homogenization through, for example, edge effects and source-sink dynamics. Smallholder plantations in our study region lie at the deforestation frontier41—other regions that have undergone earlier land-use change may consist of larger, more homogenous, intensively managed industrial plantations (not included in our study). Therefore, higher levels of homogenization and shifts from differentiation to homogenization are expected as smallholders allocate more land to the main crop42 and optimize management and logistics to increase crop profitability8,41,43 and on large-scale industrial plantations. These considerations help to identify points of intervention in existing plantations and in plantations that are entering second and third generations to increase differentiation and promote more sustainable landscapes2,3,4.

Land uses differed markedly in species composition, as shown by the ordination of mean pairwise community dissimilarities aggregated across all taxonomic groups (Fig. 3) and the analyses of similarities (ANOSIM; R = 0.92; P < 0.001). Compositional shifts from forests to monocultures were primarily associated with changes in microclimate and vegetation structure (Fig. 3). These results were corroborated by a multiple factor analysis, which identifies a common structure across two or more data matrices without assuming causal relationships44. The common structure across taxonomic groups and environmental variables aligned with land use (the first dimension explains 18% of the variance and was associated with land-use type), and was mostly driven by compositional shifts in fungi, protists, bacteria, oribatid mites, and canopy spiders and bugs (Supplementary Table 1 and Supplementary Fig. 6). A previous study, using the same plots, shows a compositional shift in terms of a loss of plant symbionts and a gain of pathogenic fungi with land-use intensification35, despite almost no change in fungal richness across land uses. Therefore, understanding compositional shifts in soil communities is highly relevant because they affect ecosystem functioning—for example, via aboveground–belowground interactions and nutrient cycling33,35.

Identifying primary drivers of biodiversity change is crucial to landscape management. Studies of β-diversity have often contrasted the roles of ecologically neutral processes with those of niche-based community assembly45,46,47. Strong contributions of geographical distance to β-diversity indicate a prevalence of neutral, dispersal-related processes, whereas strong contributions of environmental variables indicate an important role of habitat filtering48. To disentangle the relative contributions of geographical distance, environmental differences and landscape context to β-diversity, we performed generalized dissimilarity modelling (GDM)49. The GDMs explained substantial variation in β-diversity (>50%) for understorey plants, fungi, bacteria, protists, canopy spiders, beetles, bugs, parasitoids and springtails, as well as trees, archaea, butterflies and oribatid mites (Fig. 4). The variation in pairwise β-diversity was strongly related to environmental variables, particularly vegetation and litter availability, both of which vary with land-use types42. By contrast, geographic distance contributed only weakly to β-diversity for most taxonomic groups (Fig. 4). This suggests a stronger role of habitat filtering, rather than dispersal, in structuring the species assemblages in the landscape mosaic under study.
